title: The next slowest suite tests (sync e2e, live kb, leaks) each run under 6 s alone, so the whole suite keeps its darwin ceiling with sibling workers
goal: the slowest tests of _tools/test_sync_e2e.py, _tools/test_live_kb.py and _tools/test_leaks.py each run under 6 s alone in a tests.py --durations=5 run with every assertion kept, never by raising _tools/tests_ceiling.json, so a worker's whole-suite run keeps its darwin ceiling with three or four sibling workers (SP-qlpfcgs2: after the land scenarios were cut under 8 s, worker runs took 24.1 to 29 s against the 24 s ceiling with two or three siblings, all 100 passing, these files holding the slowest tests at 6.1 to 8.6 s, while SP-uzwbt63u runs took 25 to 38 s at load 7 to 8, which absorbs BG-vrijmdre's first half)

run: import re,subprocess,sys;p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/tests.py","_tools/test_sync_e2e.py","_tools/test_live_kb.py","_tools/test_leaks.py","--no-reuse","--durations=5"],capture_output=True,text=True);t=[float(x) for x in re.findall(r"^(\d+\.\d+)s call",p.stdout,re.M)];sys.exit(1 if p.returncode or not t or max(t)>=6 else 0)

gates.question: How do the slowest tests of test_sync_e2e.py, test_live_kb.py and test_leaks.py get under 6 s with every assertion kept?
options: cut work and split merged scenarios into new tests
cut work inside each test only
gates.recommendation: cut work and split merged scenarios into new tests
gates.answer: cut work and split merged scenarios into new tests

notes: Premise run 2026-10-13 (load near 1.5 on 14 cores): slowest calls 7.48, 7.28, 7.05, 6.09 s; the check exits 1. The review's whole-suite run passed on a quiet host.
